To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a powerful stakeholder, in our case the Minister of Finance, is able to influence project portfolio management in a way that is detrimental to the end user.

the presence of one strong stakeholder, the absence of a clear end user and the lack of a portfolio perspective on innovation projects in an organization lead to coordination practices that are mainly based on a project perspective and that focus on control rather than on user needs.
a powerful stakeholder, who is the only one who knows the end user, is able to control the project portfolio and ensure that the end user perspective is taken into account.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and how coordination practices can be adapted to take a user perspective in a project portfolio.
how coordination practices are affected by the presence of one master and many end users in managing a portfolio of public service innovation projects.

the following research question: How do coordination practices in a portfolio of public service innovation projects affect the ability of the organization to achieve control and user focused integration?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of one strong stakeholder and anonymous end users has an impact on coordination practices in a project portfolio.
the coordination of a portfolio of service innovations is not a straightforward matter, and it is difficult to find an optimal solution.
the presence of one master and many end users in a portfolio of innovation projects may be an obstacle to achieving a high degree of coordination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

coordination in managing a portfolio of interrelated service innovation projects can be hindered by a powerful stakeholder and invisible end users, and that this is exacerbated by the absence of a shared understanding of how coordination should be done.
the powerful stakeholder is a strong driver of coordination, whereas end users are not.

the coordination of innovation portfolios in a public service context is characterized by a high degree of centralisation and control, which is a consequence of a strong focus on efficiency and risk mitigation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
coordination of innovation projects is not only about controlling resources and mitigating risks but also about creating value for end users.
the presence of a powerful stakeholder can be used to create a shared understanding of the user perspective and thereby to coordinate a project portfolio towards a user perspective.
coordination practices in a public service portfolio of innovation projects are not only influenced by the presence of one master, but also by the presence of invisible end users.
